GM did not have a production engine program ready to deliver it on the timetable Corvette needed, so the project went outside the traditional Chevrolet powertrain organization. Lotus Engineering in Hethel, England, which GM acquired in 1986, became heavily involved in the design and development of what would become the LT5. The engine retained Chevrolet small-block bore spacing at 4.400 inches, but its architecture was otherwise radically different from the conventional Gen I small-block.

The LT5 was exotic by Corvette standards. It used an all-aluminum block and heads, a 99 mm bore and 93 mm stroke, four camshafts, four valves per cylinder, and 32 valves in total. Joe Royle’s Dogs of War arrived at the old Wembley with the semi-final demolition of Spurs behind them and survival already secured. Manchester United were the favourites, even without Cantona and with Cole and Kanchelskis unavailable. Ferguson, Schmeichel, Bruce, Pallister, Keane, Ince, Hughes — the pedigree was obvious. Everton had the hunger, the organisation, and Neville Southall.

It was short on flourish and long on blue. United started with the ball and the expectation. Everton started with the press. Parkinson and Horne snapped into midfield the way they had all spring. On the half-hour the break came. Ince lost it, Limpar switched the play, Jackson cut the ball back, and Stuart’s shot smashed off the underside of the bar. Rideout was there first. Header. 1-0. Half of Wembley erupted; the other half went quiet.

Bruce was already struggling and went at half-time. Giggs came on and United pushed. For the next forty-five minutes the game became a siege. Southall was immense — one double save from Scholes still lives in the memory. Watson organised, Ablett and Unsworth blocked, Hinchcliffe and Jackson cleared. Ferguson replaced the limping Rideout early in the second half. Amokachi came on later. Schmeichel went up for corners late on. Nothing. The final whistle blew on 90 minutes and the cup was Everton’s for the fifth time.

Watson climbed the steps. Royle had turned the season. Southall said afterwards it was for the people who had stood in the rain when things were bad. Stuart and Rideout had done the damage; Watson and Southall had made it stick. The drop had been survived. Wembley had been won.
